title: Trustworthy Machine Learning for Interpretable Early Warning of Diabetes: Modern Ensembles and Tabular Deep Learning with Causal Inference, Counterfactuals, and Uncertainty
content: Globally, an estimated 589 million adults (20-79 years) are living with diabetes,  with 1 in 9 individuals affected. Beyond traditional diagnostic and early detection  systems, machine learning is already implemented to diagnose the disease. Nev ertheless, there are several gaps that are not addressed so far. In this research, a  trustworthy machine learning framework is proposed for early warning of diabetes  that integrates causal inference, interpretability, modern ensemble methods, and  tabular deep learning to address the critical demands of reliability, fairness, and  interpretability in clinical AI systems. The study utilizes a diverse model suite  including LightGBM, XGBoost-DART, HistGBM, and TabNet, along with a  novel Causal-guided Stacking Classifier (CGSC) using LightGBM as the meta learner. Causal Forests are employed for feature selection to prioritize stable and  causally-relevant predictors in this particular model. For interpretability, SHAP  is leveraged to provide global, local, and mean feature attribution for the best performing ensemble, while TabNet’s built-in attention mechanism is used to  highlight local explanations and feature salience. As a basic fairness-aware design  choice, gender was excluded as a feature to examine bias mitigation without  compromising performance. Uncertainty quantification of the ensemble models  is also provided. Counterfactuals are added for personalized disease prevention  attempts. Our results indicate that the CGSC achieved the highest recall (0.81)  with minimal F1-score uncertainty (0.73 ± 0.03), demonstrating strong predic tive reliability. All experiments are fully reproducible, with resources available  at the GitHub repository.
